## Things your lead should know before shipping

None of these require restructuring or a second skill.

**1. The description decides when the skill loads, and this one is too vague.**
Claude chooses whether to load a skill based only on its description. "Anything related to our company" doesn't mention alerts, deploys, or style rules. So it may not load when someone pastes a `HighErrorRate` alert, and it may load for unrelated chat. This is a one-line fix you can drop in with no extra work:

```yaml
description: Internal company handbook. Use for Python/TypeScript code style, deploying or rolling back our 4 services (<names>), on-call alert response (runbook for all 35 alerts), PTO and expense policy, brand voice for marketing copy, org chart and contacts, and definitions of internal terms/jargon.
```

**2. The whole file is loaded every time the skill triggers.**
At about 3,000 lines (roughly 30–40k tokens), a glossary lookup pulls in the entire on-call runbook and the expense policy too. Anthropic's guidance is to keep SKILL.md under about 500 lines. You can fix this later and still have one skill. Move each section into its own file in the same skill folder (`runbook.md`, `style.md`, etc.), and have SKILL.md list which file covers what. Claude then reads only the file it needs. It's worth doing once the costs or slow responses become noticeable.

**3. The org chart has personal phone numbers.**
Anything in the skill can be read by Claude and repeated in any conversation where the skill loads, including marketing-copy sessions. It also goes stale quickly. Consider keeping names and roles but linking to your directory for phone numbers. At minimum, confirm that's okay with whoever owns that data.

If the answer is "ship it as-is today," the version above is ready. I'd still recommend swapping in the description from item 1, since that costs nothing and improves how reliably the skill triggers.
